anti_overlap: fd-indie-game-marketplace-launch covers the distribution and launch mechanics of the skill — this agent covers the play-session design quality and scenario format stability, not the marketplace strategy

fd-wargaming-scenario-validity covers whether the scenario's forcing functions reliably surface alignment-relevant decisions — this agent covers the facilitated-play experience quality and session management rules for the chat-gateway mode
fd-clinical-trial-data-monitoring covers the kill-gate and data integrity mechanics — this agent covers the session lifecycle and replay mechanics that produce the play experience
decision_lens: A rule set that cannot be consistently adjudicated by independent session facilitators without consulting the designer is not a published product — it is a draft, and should be labeled and distributed accordingly.
distance_rationale: TTRPG line editors manage the exact combination of problems ShadowBench's play mode faces: a rule system that must produce consistent outcomes when facilitated by strangers without designer intervention, replay value through scenario branching, session state portability across rule editions, and multi-participant session ownership models. The field has decades of practice on exactly the 'single-owner vs. multi-participant' session problem and the 'mid-campaign edition change' compatibility problem that the PRD identifies as open questions.
expected_isomorphisms: GM-facing encounter description quality → Hermes narration quality for play-mode decision points
Multi-participant table ownership rules → single-owner Discord session with spectators model
Mid-campaign edition change → session JSONL resume across binary version updates
Living rulebook format stability → RON scenario format as public standard vs. internal format
Replay value through branching adventure design → early-choice-keyed event divergence in the Amaran scenario
focus: Whether the dual bench+play mode design has sufficient replay mechanics, session ownership rules, and scenario format stability to sustain repeated use and community-generated content without fragmenting the scoring canon
name: fd-tabletop-rpg-publication
persona: Apply the perspective of a tabletop RPG line editor who has managed multi-edition game systems with living rulebooks and organized-play programs — they care about whether the rules as written produce the intended play experience at the table, measure rulebook ambiguity reports and session facilitator friction, and flag any design that creates unsolvable table conflicts or orphans earlier content under new rule editions.
review_areas: Session ownership model ambiguity (F4): the PRD defers multi-user Discord play to v1.1 but ships v1 with 'single-owner-only (others can spectate but their messages don't advance state)' — this creates a rule that is invisible to players until they collide with it mid-session; the spec needs explicit player-facing language explaining ownership semantics before the session starts, not after state fails to advance

Replay value mechanism is an open question at PRD stage (OQ4): the PRD acknowledges this is unresolved ('is it RNG seed variation, branching events keyed to early choices, or something else') and defers to planning — but the F4 acceptance criteria already specify 'at least one binary branching point in the first 5 decisions' without locking the mechanism, creating a scenario spec that cannot be validated before F4 starts

Scenario format as a published standard: the PRD references 'RON file' for scenario format but the skill ships a single hardcoded Amaran scenario — the PRD does not specify whether the RON format is a public standard that community members can use to create scenarios, or a private internal format; this decision affects whether the skill becomes a platform or a single-scenario product

v0.1-preview vs. LOCKED scoring compatibility: the trace re-scoring compatibility table (§trace re-scoring) defines which protocol changes orphan v1 traces — but the PRD does not specify what the skill does when a user runs /shadow-work rescore on a v1 trace against a future LOCKED scorer; the error message, deprecation warning, and migration path need to be designed before v1 ships to avoid the equivalent of 'your 1st-edition character sheet doesn't work in 2nd edition' surprise

Decision-point narration quality as a gating requirement: F4 specifies session end-state criteria (kill-gate or max-turn cap) but not narration quality standards — in TTRPG publishing, the quality of the GM-facing encounter descriptions is a primary review criterion because poor narration produces table friction even when the underlying mechanics are correct; the Hermes narration output is not in scope for any F4 acceptance criterion

Session resume across message interruptions: F4 specifies that session state persists in a JSONL file for resume — but does not specify what happens when a player resumes a session after the Hermes skill has been updated to a new binary version; a session started on v0.1-preview against one binary may be unresumable against a newer binary, equivalent to the classic TTRPG 'mid-campaign edition change' problem

severity_examples.condition: When F4's 'single-owner-only' rule is not surfaced to all thread participants at session start with explicit language about who controls the session
severity_examples.scenario: A Discord thread with 4 participants starts a /shadow-work play session; three players send messages expecting their choices to advance the scenario; the session silently ignores all but the session owner's messages; the play experience collapses in confusion with no in-game explanation of ownership rules

severity_examples.condition: When OQ4 (replay-value mechanism) is resolved as RNG variation without validating that the mechanism produces arc-level differentiation rather than surface-level event variation
severity_examples.scenario: The replay branching mechanism is implemented as RNG seed variation (every run is a fresh random seed) rather than as early-choice-keyed event branching — two replays of the same scenario have different events but not meaningfully different arcs; the 'replay value' acceptance criterion is met technically but fails qualitatively for the Bob persona who expects choices to matter

severity_examples.condition: When the session JSONL schema has no versioning field and the binary has no session-schema migration path for resume operations
severity_examples.scenario: A user resumes a play session started on binary v1.0.0 using binary v1.0.2; the session JSONL contains state fields that have been renamed in the newer binary; the resume silently initializes missing fields to defaults, producing a scenario that diverges from the player's prior state with no warning

source_domain: Tabletop RPG line editing and organized-play program management
success_hints: The session intro message for /shadow-work play always includes explicit ownership framing: 'This session is controlled by @<owner>. Other participants can observe but their messages will not advance the scenario.' — this is displayed before the scenario begins, not as an error after a failed non-owner action

OQ4 (replay-value mechanism) is resolved before F4 implementation starts with a documented test: run the scenario twice with different early choices and verify that the available event sets diverge meaningfully by turn 10 — the mechanism must pass this test before F4 is marked ready
The session JSONL schema includes a version field from v1.0.0; the binary checks this field on resume and either migrates the session or prints an explicit compatibility warning before proceeding
task_context: ShadowBench's Hermes skill ships a chat-gateway play mode (F4) where users make 8-12 decisions in a scenario over ~25 minutes in Discord/Slack/Telegram. The PRD defers multi-user session ownership to v1.1 and leaves the replay-value mechanism as an open question.
